parallel.requirements: The prompt required every file under /workspace/requirements to be read and all 48 listed requirement slugs to be implemented with non-empty per-slug patches.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent wrote a 48-node plan and launched a first wave of 27 parallel subagents over 40 requirements, using scoped child briefs and later outer-loop continuation rounds.
parallel.implementation: Subagents committed many focused ECharts changes, and later rounds completed the remaining patch set; the final harness collected 48 requirement patch files.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The shared repository was the integration target, with child commits and per-requirement diff files forming the deliverable; no final response text was written.
parallel.verification: Children used mostly focused jest and tsc checks, then the harness ran direct tests after collecting all patches and reported four case failures plus the pytest tail.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Coverage reached 48/48 patches, but official unit cases 21147, 21347, 21380, and 21410 still failed, so implementation defects remained despite full coverage.

serial.requirements: The same prompt and 48 requirement list were available to the serial control, with the same instruction to address all requirements before finishing.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial run used a single main-agent trajectory without AgentSwarm calls or subagents and iterated across three outer-loop rounds.
serial.implementation: The serial agent implemented and committed 29 requirement patches by the third round, leaving 19 required patch files absent at final collection.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The single workspace and sequential commits avoided child handoff and shared-live-write issues, but the delivered patch set was incomplete.
serial.verification: The serial run produced only three agent test files and then direct run-tests failed; official results show 13 case failures plus the pytest tail.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Serial timed out before covering every requirement and also left incorrect behavior among implemented areas, finishing with only 15 of 28 official unit cases passing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel saw the full 48-slug requirement list in the prompt and in outer-loop progress state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial saw the identical full 48-slug requirement list and had the same completion and patch requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The requirement surface was the same; the difference was execution coverage, not task understanding at the prompt level.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed the task into a 27-subagent wave covering 40 requirements with scoped ownership and later continuation rounds.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial remained a single-agent control with no AgentSwarm calls and no subagent ownership split.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used broad delegated ownership; serial used sequential ownership by one main agent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs included requirement details, file hints, and concurrency rules to avoid package-level and file-scope interference.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-interface boundary; task context stayed in the main session and outer-loop prompts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit parent-child context and workspace coordination boundaries; serial did not expose those boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced all 48 required patch files by the final collection point.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced 29 required patch files by the final collection point.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel completed far more implementation surface, while serial left many requirements without patch artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel round 1 was explicitly cancelled with active child work, and the AgentSwarm result reported 23 completed and 4 aborted children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its rounds ended by agent timeout as a single control trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child cancellation and resume/takeover mechanics; serial had ordinary single-agent timeout progression.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote into a shared live workspace, and reports mention unrelated in-progress edits or failing tests from other agents affecting verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had actual_parallel_used false and zero subagents, so there were no parallel shared-workspace write boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel carried shared-live-workspace instability; serial avoided that class but was slower and incomplete.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel collected 40 agent test files and ran direct run-tests, but the official result still failed four case tests plus the pytest tail.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial collected three agent test files and direct run-tests failed with 13 case failures plus the pytest tail.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had broader local verification and fewer official failures; serial had less verification depth and more uncovered or broken cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed a large token/tool budget but recovered across three rounds, reaching 100 percent patch coverage before official tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also ran three rounds but remained at 60.4 percent requirement coverage before final tests and had an agent_timeout failure mode.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent much more budget to buy coverage; serial exhausted its serial work window before most remaining requirements were implemented.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both runs are unresolved. Parallel materially outperformed serial on coverage and case pass count, reaching 48 of 48 patch artifacts and 24 of 28 case passes, while serial reached 29 patches and 15 of 28 case passes. The remaining parallel failures are best treated as ordinary implementation defects in completed work, with the retained parallel coordination patterns contributing adverse process cost rather than explaining a different pass/fail result.
parallel_contributors: Parallel fan-out plus continuation rounds achieved full 48-patch coverage before evaluation.
Round-1 child cancellation and shared-workspace verification noise were adverse process episodes but did not create a discordant outcome.
serial_contributors: Serial control had no delegation and progressed sequentially to only 29 patch files before timeout.
Serial official results show more failing cases, consistent with incomplete requirement coverage plus coding defects.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel still failed tests 21147, 21347, 21380, and 21410 despite complete patch coverage.
Serial failed those and nine additional case tests while also lacking 19 requirement patch artifacts.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; comparative contributors and retained patterns are not claimed as an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The round-1 parent launched a live AgentSwarm and then the active turn was explicitly cancelled before all children completed. The returned swarm result reports completed: 23, aborted: 4 and includes a resume hint, so the stopped children were still unfinished. This caused round 1 to close with 14 requirements still remaining, although later rounds took over enough work to reach 48 patch files.
candidates.realized_consequence: Four live child scopes were aborted in round 1, leaving 14 of 48 requirements for later rounds instead of returning complete child work in the first wave.
candidates.near_match_reason: The aborted scopes were not abandoned through closure; later rounds reduced the remaining list to zero and the harness collected all 48 patches.

candidates.reason: Rejected: no complete promotable candidate is shown waiting unplaced at closure; the observed lifecycle issue is cancellation before some child work finalized.
Rejected: the harness ran direct tests after collecting all 48 patches; no child result is shown merged only after the relevant integrated verification without a retest.
Rejected: completed child implementations were committed into the shared workspace and collected as patches; aborted children were unfinished rather than completed-but-unjoined.
Rejected: no verifier child produced a concrete finding trapped below the parent before closure; the AgentSwarm aggregate result did return.
Rejected: aborted or remaining round-1 scopes were later resumed or reworked, and final harness collection reached all 48 requirement patches.
Rejected: no concrete completed child result is shown available to the parent and then ignored in an inconsistent decision.
Rejected: the record shows timeout/cancellation, but not a parent waiting without inspecting available progress or partial results that would alter action.
Rejected: concurrent agents touched different areas, but no competing cross-file design ownership requiring reconciliation is directly proven.
Rejected: no direct same-file concurrent edit event with observed reconciliation or conflict is proven.
Rejected: no non-entry source file produced or owned by one live agent is shown being wholesale replaced by another.
Rejected: no executable, entry-point source, or submitted artifact is shown being replaced while another agent owned or used it.
Rejected: no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion is shown replacing multiple final outputs and invalidating provenance.

The parent launched 27 concurrent subagents into the same /workspace and had to warn them that other agents were editing it. Subagent reports then show concrete unstable-state effects: tests and type checks were narrowed because other agents had failing or in-progress files and uncommitted edits. No direct same-file collision or overwrite is proven, so the supported write label is the unisolated shared-workspace form.
candidates.realized_consequence: Shared live edits made intermediate verification and provenance unstable, so children used focused checks and path-specific staging instead of reliable full-suite validation.
candidates.near_match_reason: The record shows shared-workspace interference, but it does not prove that two live agents edited the same file and reconciled one another.

candidates.reason: Rejected: other agents created tests and intermediate files, but no generated artifact, cache, process, or fixture from one actor is shown consumed as stable input by another.
